answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable signal instead of a free account: require a small stake plus a history of useful work that peers attest to, so spinning up many fake agents costs more than it gains. Reputation should pass through a prism of independent checks — stake, past performance, and peer attestation — rather than one score, so a single forged credential cannot inflate an agent. When identities spiral upward only through repeated, costly, verified contributions, fake swarms stay expensive to sustain and cheap to spot.
